description: Bengal Hydro Detective pairs a 24-year NASA Earth observation pipeline (2002–2026) with an offline web workbench to track water storage trends across Bangladesh. It helps students, researchers, and water planners inspect significant storage decline across regions home to 108.5 million residents (-1.25 cm/yr in the Northwest) while separating long-term drawdown from short-window variability and spurious reanalysis rainfall trends.
summary: Bengal Hydro Detective is an offline-capable web workbench and 24-year hydroclimatic audit built around Dr. James Acker's 5-step trend workflow for Bangladesh (2002–2026). It helps students, researchers, and water planners distinguish real long-term changes in water storage, rainfall, and air quality from short-window noise and model artifacts. Users pick a NASA satellite or land-surface variable (GRACE/GRACE-FO, GPM IMERG, GLDAS, MODIS, AERONET, AIRS, or OMI), select a macro-region or division, and inspect live Theil-Sen slopes, 95% confidence bounds, and Hurwicz-corrected Effective-Sample-Size Mann-Kendall tests directly in the browser.
details:
The challenge it answers

Short 8-year GRACE-FO windows (2018–2026, p = 0.0549) hide storage trends beneath monsoon variability, while a +45% to +84% step break around 2014–2015 in NASA POWER creates spurious rainfall slopes. Extending CSR GRACE/GRACE-FO to 24 years (2002–2026) alongside GPM IMERG and GLDAS identifies significant total water storage decline across regions home to 108.5 million people (-1.25 cm/yr, q < 0.0001 in the Northwest), while satellite rainfall shows no detectable trend and subtracting 0–2 m soil moisture places the drawdown in the unpartitioned residual.

How it works

Bengal Hydro Detective feeds 24 years of GRACE/GRACE-FO gravimetry, GPM IMERG and POWER rain, GLDAS soil moisture, AIRS/OMI atmospheric, MODIS/AERONET aerosol, and GPWv4/MCD12Q1 land records into a Hurwicz-corrected Effective-Sample-Size Mann-Kendall and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR pipeline calibrated across 2,000 Monte Carlo runs (5.0–5.8% false-positive rate). A zero-backend vanilla JavaScript workbench runs that statistical engine offline in the browser across an interactive SVG map, time-series and seasonal charts with 95% confidence fans, and 7 guided case studies verified for Python-to-JavaScript parity.

What we'd build next

Automating monthly NASA Earthdata ingestion alongside Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) well hydrographs and Barind Multipurpose Development Authority (BMDA) metered pumping or electricity records would separate groundwater extraction from surface water storage. Downscaling ~300 km GRACE gravimetry and 1.0° AIRS grids to local administrative units would then let dry-season storage alerts guide water-saving practices such as Alternate Wetting and Drying and managed recharge.
